name: betterleaks-suppression-audit-reports
instr:
Gitleaks cannot explain why each detected secret candidate was emitted or suppressed. Add opt-in suppression auditing across detection and reporting without exposing raw secrets. Keep audited output correlated, ordered, balanced, and compatible with ordinary reporting.

Every observed candidate has one stable `DecisionID` and exactly one terminal `Decision`, classified by `DecisionKind` and `DecisionOutcome` in observation order, even when validation completes out of order. Decisions distinguish emission outcomes, inline allow comments, expression filters, confidence thresholds, ignored fingerprints, baselines, and validation filters. `AuditedResult` preserves each completed decision once when scanning fails or is cancelled and reports the failure separately.

`AuditReport.Validate` returns `ErrInvalidAudit`, exactly `errors.New("invalid audit report")`, unless totals, decisions, and findings balance one-to-one. Redaction changes only retained findings, not audit identity, classification, ordering, or totals. Mixed emitted and suppressed candidates must retain observation order and correlations. A baseline suppression must have the same safe identity and kind in every renderer.

Through `cmd.reporterForCommand`, `Reporter.Write` retains established bytes, empty behavior, and command outcomes. `Reporter.WriteAudit` renders JSON, CSV, JUnit, SARIF, or templates without changing shared accounting. CSV audit output deterministically represents summaries, emitted findings, and sup
